note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, court kind, lighting answer and hours line below comes from one City of Albuquerque page: its pickleball page, whose "Pickleball Court Locations" table gives each venue a name, an address and a description cell, with a few sentences of prose beneath it on hours, reservations, the ninety-minute rule and lessons. Where the City stays silent, on price, surface, parking, indoor or outdoor, and lighting at twelve of the thirteen venues, this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking:
The City of Albuquerque publishes nothing about parking at any of the thirteen venues. The word does not appear on the pickleball page at all. Restrooms are not mentioned either, at any venue.

What the City does publish that shapes a trip is the address. It writes almost all of them without a street type, such as "501 Elizabeth SE" and "7511 Burke NE", and the US Census address file supplied one for each: Elizabeth Street, Cherokee Road, Burke Street. All thirteen matched at house-number level, with the compass quadrant carried through unchanged.
slots.peak_hours:
The City states hours for two published venues and a rule for all of them. The hours line reads "Manzano Mesa, Villella, and Pat Hurley are open from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily", and Pat Hurley is not published here, so it covers Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex and Villela Pickleball Courts. The other eleven venues have no stated hours at all.

The rule sits under "Availability & Reservations": "Courts are typically available on a first come, first serve basis and play is limited to 1.5 hours when others are waiting." Sierra Vista Tennis Complex is the one venue whose courts the City says can be booked, "in advanced by calling 505-767-5445". Whole complexes can be reserved for tournaments through the City's Sports Office. The City does not publish when any venue is busy.
slots.surface_condition:
The City names no surface for any pickleball court in Albuquerque. No cell of the table says asphalt, concrete or acrylic, and nothing says indoor or outdoor about any venue.

What the City does state, in the description cell of every row but one, is what kind of court is being counted. Two venues are a "Pickleball Complex", Manzano Mesa with thirty-three courts and Villela with six, and the prose calls them the City's "two dedicated pickleball complexes". Nine venues are "Tennis Courts with Pickleball Lines", and the count in those cells is of pickleball courts marked out, not of tennis courts. Sierra Vista is "Tennis/Pickleball Courts" with "2 Courts and 4 Lined Courts". Wells Park's cell says "3 Pickleball Courts" and nothing about their kind, so that one is recorded as unstated. Nets are not mentioned on the visible page.
slots.local_scene:
Eighty-six courts across thirteen City venues, thirty-nine of them at the two dedicated complexes and the rest across eleven parks. Albuquerque is the first New Mexico city on this site and the first in Bernalillo County. Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex's thirty-three courts is the largest single-venue count on this site. Eighty-six is one of the largest court totals on the site, second to Seattle's ninety-two.

The City's page names a City Pickleball Manager, 505-224-6693, runs junior and adult lessons at Manzano Mesa with classes "limited to six participants", and describes the ABQ Pickleball Club as a body that "provides tournaments, training, playing opportunities, and conducts pickleball open houses". None of that is a schedule of open play; no open-play time is published for any venue.

Three venues the City lists are not published, and they are named here rather than dropped: Pat Hurley Park, Alamosa Park and Ventana Ranch Park. Neither the US Census address file nor OpenStreetMap finds the address the City writes for any of the three. That costs twenty-eight courts, twenty of them lit.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts, with lights and stated hours
best_for.text: Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex has thirty-three dedicated courts, twenty-one of them lit, open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily in the City's own sentence, at 501 Elizabeth SE. It is the City's lesson venue and the one Albuquerque address where a rotation, an evening game and a stated closing time all rest on published facts. Price, surface and parking are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you want dedicated courts at a smaller complex
best_for.text: Villela Pickleball Courts is the second of the City's "two dedicated pickleball complexes": six courts that are pickleball courts whenever you arrive, open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily, at 4800 Cherokee NE. Six is enough for a rotation. The City states no lighting here, so the late end of those hours is not stated; price and surface are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to book a court in advance
best_for.text: Sierra Vista Tennis Complex is the one Albuquerque venue whose courts the City says can be reserved, "in advanced by calling 505-767-5445". Two permanent pickleball courts and four lined onto tennis courts, six in all, at 5001 Montano Rd. NW. No price is stated for a reservation, no hours are stated for the complex, and lighting is not stated.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Albuquerque have?
faqs.a: We list 86 across thirteen City venues: 33 at Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex, 8 at Lauren C. Bolles, 6 each at Villela, Sierra Vista and Montgomery, 4 each at Columbus, Eagle Ranch, Loma Del Norte, Lynnewood and Quintessence, 3 at Wells Park and 2 each at Hoffman and Rinconada.
Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex, where the City's cell reads "33 Courts (21 Lighted)": twenty-one lit, twelve with no statement. No other published venue carries a lighting answer either way.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Albuquerque?
faqs.a: Not stated, at any venue. The City publishes no price for any pickleball court; "first come, first serve" describes how a court is taken, not what it costs, and the phone reservation at Sierra Vista carries no stated fee.
